Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certificates; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for incorporation registration.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July (Approved Text of the Spanish Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital), articles 4 (minimum capital), 20–32 (incorporation procedure), 62 (in-kind contribution valuation), and 75–78 (share subscription and payment).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de constitución (public deed of incorporation) submitted for registration in the Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 29 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

For the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the statutory minimum capital is €3,000. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid in cash or attested in-kind contributions as evidenced by a bank certificate ('certificado bancario de desembolso') or expert report. The funds are held in escrow until the company's registration is entered in the Mercantile Registry.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification from a competent technician and municipal advisor (including evacuation signs, fire extinguishers and emergency lighting); occupational risk prevention assessment under Law 31/1995; municipal 'licencia de apertura' (opening license) for the office premises in which the platform is operated; where applicable, accessibility and building structural compatibility clearance.

Paid-in capital rule: For the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the statutory minimum capital is €3,000. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid in cash or attested in-kind contributions as evidenced by a bank certificate ('certificado bancario de desembolso') or expert report. The funds are held in escrow until the company's registration is entered in the Mercantile Registry.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED: that the statutes of the company are adopted; that the total share capital of €3,000 is approved, fully subscribed and paid in cash by the founding member; that the registered office of the company is established at Carrer de la Pau 12, Barcelona, Spain; that the director appointed by the founding member is the undersigned and accepts office; that the director is authorized to effect all filings with the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities, and to apply for the necessary crowdfunding service provider authorization.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Sede Electrónica — sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs matters shared with Dependencia Regional de Aduanas under AEAT.

E-government filing portal

A non-resident founder must (i) execute the SL deed before a Spanish Notary with an appointed tax representative; (ii) file the pre-incorporation NIF application on Form 030; (iii) within one month of deed registration (Registro Mercantil), file Form 036 (alta en el Censo de Empresarios) to declare commencement of activity and register for IVA, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, and the IAE (economic activities tax); (iv) obtain the definitive NIF issued by AEAT with format B/R + 8 digits for the legal entity; and (v) for the regulated equity crowdfunding scope, obtain CNMV authorisation under Law 5/2015 as a condition to exercising the licensed activity; AEAT census registration precedes or coexists with authorisation for tax-ID issuance purposes.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — SL is an opaque resident taxpayer fully subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014, LIS) on worldwide income at a 25% standard rate (15% for newly created companies in the first two taxable periods on qualifying business income under Art. 29.1 LIS); no pass-through or fiscal transparency applies; territorial scope is the whole Spanish mainland, including Islas Baleares/Canarias (with Canary Islands-specific tax offset mechanisms); no tax-exempt zone status. — A non-resident founder must (i) execute the SL deed before a Spanish Notary with an appointed tax representative; (ii) file the pre-incorporation NIF application on Form 030; (iii) within one month of deed registration (Registro Mercantil), file Form 036 (alta en el Censo de Empresarios) to declare commencement of activity and register for IVA, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, and the IAE (economic activities tax); (iv) obtain the definitive NIF issued by AEAT with format B/R + 8 digits for the legal entity; and (v) for the regulated equity crowdfunding scope, obtain CNMV authorisation under Law 5/2015 as a condition to exercising the licensed activity; AEAT census registration precedes or coexists with authorisation for tax-ID issuance purposes.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — SL is an opaque resident taxpayer fully subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014, LIS) on worldwide income at a 25% standard rate (15% for newly created companies in the first two taxable periods on qualifying business income under Art. 29.1 LIS); no pass-through or fiscal transparency applies; territorial scope is the whole Spanish mainland, including Islas Baleares/Canarias (with Canary Islands-specific tax offset mechanisms); no tax-exempt zone status.

Available election forms

Spain does not provide a check-the-box election. Available statutory elections: (i) group VAT registration as a single taxable person (Régimen de Grupo de Entidades, Art. 68 LIVA) upon AEAT approval; (ii) consolidated corporate tax group election under Arts. 62-67 LIS (permanent election for the parent and its 75%-owned qualifying Spanish subsidiaries); (iii) ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) holding-regime election under Art. 21 ETR for foreign shareholding/royalty streams; (iv) application of the SME special rules (reserva de capitalización and minoración por incentivos) under Arts. 104-105 LIS; and (v) no hybrid-mismatch election exists — ATAD 1 (Law 11/2016) and ATAD 2 (implementing rules) automatically deny deductions on non-deductible double-dip arrangements and reverse import mismatch structures by operation of law without elective relief.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 — any taxable person habitually performing taxable supplies in Spain must register for IVA from the first euro of activity; no general small-trader exemption applies; intra-Community distance sales and OSS B2C digital services crossing the EUR 10,000 annual threshold to Spanish consumers require Spanish VAT registration via the EU OSS portal; the crowdfunding platform's separate financing services (commissions for issuer onboarding, investor admission fees, and escrow management) are taxable supplies without threshold exemption.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Export of goods to non-EU destinations qualifies for the 0% rate where the goods physically leave Spanish customs territory within detectable tracking and the exporter/representative obtains authentic export evidence (DUA depósito previo or regular declaration with numero de referencia definitivo). For services: (i) B2B supply to a non-resident entrepreneur is outside Spanish VAT (reverse charge in recipient's EU country if EU; zero-rated if outside EU), and (ii) B2C supply of crowdfunding platform services (issuer listing fees, investor matching and data intermediation, administrative handling) to consumers resident outside the EU falls outside Spanish VAT under Art. 70.1 LIVA provided the recipient is non-EU; intra-EU B2C services remain taxable at 21% by Spain as the place of establishment; zero-rating/out-of-scope eligibility must be supported by identification certificates of the recipient (VAT ID for EU B2B recipients, passport or residence certificate for non-EU B2C) and the platform's internal billing evidence of cross-border contract terms.

  • DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) stapled export declaration accepted and stamped/cleared by Spanish Customs (Aduana de Salida) evidencing definitive export and exit from EU territory
  • Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (conocimiento de embarque / carta de porte aéreo) naming the Spanish exporter as consignor with the actual non-EU consignee
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de ingreso/remesa de divisas) issued by the Spanish banking entity showing receipt of the exported value from the foreign buyer in convertible foreign currency

Mandatory electronic invoicing for B2B under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) with implementing Royal Decree (RD 1007/2023) — digital invoice generation through VeriFactu-compliant software, signature with AEAT-accredited digital codes, QR/DataMatrix stamping on each invoice, and near-real-time transmission to AEAT's electronic clearance service via REST API/SOAP web services; taxpayer affected by SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) — mandatory for groups in VAT-group regime and large taxpayers (turnover > EUR 6,000,000) — must submit carry-in/out books within 4 days (working) of issue/receipt; non-SII taxpayers must file Form 340/347 or the periodic Form 303/390 with book records in the new e-invoicing format once the phased implementation concludes in late 2025/2026.

Under Arts. 183-206 LGT, false export zero-rating triggers a VAT assessment retroactively re-characterising income as domestic taxable supplies: interest on late payment accrues from the original liability date; the tax penalty falls in the very-serious bracket at 50%-150% of the omitted VAT per Art. 191 LGT; refusal to refund export VAT and immediate issue of a recovery assessment; criminal liability under Art. 305 Código Penal when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single year (prison terms up to 5 years), with AEAT's Anti-Fraud Unit (Unidad de Auditoría de los Impuestos de Comercio Exterior y aduanas) systematically cross-matching SII records, bank remittance records (EDIFACT SWIFT), and customs DUA registers; proof, when obtained fraudulently or forged, is void and the 5-year time-bar is suspended during criminal proceedings.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains full liberalisation of current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Royal Decree 1816/1991, and the EOF regulation framework. The euro is fully convertible with no prior administrative authorisation; dividend repatriation, liquidation proceeds, and capital withdrawals are unrestricted in any currency. Operational hurdles are limited to: (i) the statutory 19% withholding tax on outbound non-resident dividends (treaty relief available under the applicable DTT); and (ii) post-event statistical declarations to the Banco de España Foreign Investment Registry for foreign investments equal to or exceeding EUR 3,000,000, transactions in reserved sectors, or those financed through resident debt instruments. No transfer-pricing or exchange-control clearance is required for profit remittance.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Not applicable. Spain imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no obligation to repatriate export receivables. Resident entities may hold and freely manage foreign-currency proceeds in any EUR account or foreign-currency account maintained with an authorised credit institution. Only balance-of-payments statistical reporting applies: the resident payee must report foreign-currency settlements exceeding EUR 10,000 through the bank's declared channel (to Banco de España) within five business days following the settlement, and the bank must retain the underlying transaction documentation under Funds Transfer Regulation (EU) 2015/847.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national competent authority, with the European Central Bank (ECB) retaining monetary policy and sole foreign reserve authority within the Eurosystem. Foreign investment statistical control is delegated to the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise), while the SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales) acts as the Financial Intelligence Unit.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Medium for operational payment routing; Low for escrow substitution. Legal constraints: under Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR), crowdfunding client funds must be safeguarded either in a segregated account (cuenta de terceros) held at a credit institution within the meaning of Article 4(1)(1) CRR, or by insurance, or exclusively in safe low-risk assets. An electronic money institution (Entidad de Dinero Electrónico under PSD2) is not an authorised credit institution and therefore cannot act as the statutory escrow vault for investor funds. Offshore (non-Spanish) EMIs may only access Spanish rails via PSD2 passporting, branch registration with Banco de España under Article 46 Directive (EU) 2015/2366, or by becoming a sponsored direct participant in SEPA Clearing. Post-Brexit UK EMIs retain no passport and are treated as third-country providers; they may offer ancillary collection accounts but cannot legally perform the escrow safeguarding function for an authorised Spanish ECSP.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Sectoral high-risk classification: equity crowdfunding portal licensed under ECSPR and exposing the bank to third-party investor moneys flowing into the SL's segregated accounts

Root cause: Sectoral high-risk classification: equity crowdfunding portal licensed under ECSPR and exposing the bank to third-party investor moneys flowing into the SL's segregated accounts

Defense evidence: CNMV authorisation certificate under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503; SEPBLAC-approved AML/CFT compliance manual; internal audit opinion on the portal's fund-safeguarding controls; board resolution adopting the AML policy and designating the responsible person (órgano de control); a written description of the cuenta de terceros segregation and reconciliation procedure; professional liability insurance policy for the platform's directors.
Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (e.g., USA or Latin-American shareholders) and an ownership chain with intermediate foreign holding entities, triggering enhanced due diligence under Article 9 of Law 10/2010

Root cause: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (e.g., USA or Latin-American shareholders) and an ownership chain with intermediate foreign holding entities, triggering enhanced due diligence under Article 9 of Law 10/2010

Defense evidence: Certified passport copies of each UBO; individual source-of-funds evidence (bank statements for a 12-month window, tax returns, employment or divestment instruments); a notarised and apostilled corporate chain-of-ownership chart; sworn Spanish translation of the SL Registro Mercantil extract; executed UBO declaration (form prepared per Banco de España guidance) confirming that no Politically Exposed Person status applies.
High-velocity inbound investor wire volume converging into a single escrow account, creating potential money-laundering or fraud-transmission exposure for the bank

Root cause: High-velocity inbound investor wire volume converging into a single escrow account, creating potential money-laundering or fraud-transmission exposure for the bank

Defense evidence: Transactional monitoring and sanction-screening architecture of the portal; investor source-of-funds policy for commitments above EUR 1,000; transaction-subledger reconciliation protocol evidenced by an ISAE 3402 or similar assurance report; the portal's STR/SAR escalation procedures directly linked to SEPBLAC; the platform's contractual terms confirming that client funds are returned if the funding target is not met and that no loans or civil-law confusion of investor funds can occur.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant protocol for capital injection into the ES_SL: (i) the foreign shareholder issues a SWIFT MT103 (or SWIFT to the Spanish bank's correspondents) naming the SL as beneficiary with the exact ECB/ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPC' (Capital Payments) or 'INVS' (Investment and Securities) in tag 70; (ii) the narrative field must quote the notarial deed number and date of the capital increase and indicate the Registered Merchant Registry filing; (iii) the receiving bank requires the documentary verification package comprising the notarised deed, the originator's bank statement evidencing the source of funds, and the UBO identification declaration; (iv) for investments equal to or above EUR 3,000,000, the SL must file the Foreign Investment Registry statistical declaration (Form DP-4) and submit the acknowledgement to the bank prior to credit release. Crowd-investor funds are routed separately into the segregated escrow account and are never classified as capital injection unless formally converted into equity; each investor wire must carry the payer's full legal identity, the issuance reference code, and purpose 'MCMT' (cash management) with a clear narrative identifying the crowdfunding campaign.Outbound disbursements to project owners (issuer startups) are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in EUR for domestic and EU-EEA issuers, with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) available for same-day settlement where the issuer's bank is a subscriber. Cross-border disbursements to non-EEA issuers (including select Latin-American jurisdictions) are cleared via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 documentary purpose 'CORT' (trade settlement) or 'TRAD' (trade-related), always instructed with field 71A SHA to control correspondent fees. Commercial Letters of Credit are legally inapplicable to equity-crowdfunding proceeds and are excluded from the operating treasury rails; such instruments would only be relevant if the SL later acquires a trading subsidiary, in which case a separate documentary credit policy would be established. Every disbursement is subject to the ECSPR 20-business-day transfer obligation and must include the MLRO's signed disbursement authorization evidencing the campaign's funding-target achievement and the issuer's satisfying all onboarding verifications.Plain-vanilla FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) executed with the Tier-1 domestic bank or EU counterparty under ISDA 2002 or the bank's local framework agreement, covering only the platform's own operating-income exposure (not investor positions).Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted Latin-American currencies (BRL, MXN, CLP, COP) traded with a licensed Spanish credit institution or EU investment firm, subject to internal hedging-policy limits and EMIR Article 10 reporting where the SL remains below the clearing threshold as a Non-Financial Counterparty.Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/BRL) for balance-sheet hedging of multi-currency operational liabilities, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the bank's global markets desk and subject to the counterparty credit-limit approval of the SL's treasury committee.FX Options (plain European-style calls and puts on EURUSD) purchased only as defined-risk premium structures for pipeline exposure, expressly avoiding exotic or structured barrier trades that could trigger speculative accounting treatment under IFRS 9 and additional capital-rationale demands by the bank's product governance.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational payment routing; Low for escrow substitution. Legal constraints: under Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR), crowdfunding client funds must be safeguarded either in a segregated account (cuenta de terceros) held at a credit institution within the meaning of Article 4(1)(1) CRR, or by insurance, or exclusively in safe low-risk assets. An electronic money institution (Entidad de Dinero Electrónico under PSD2) is not an authorised credit institution and therefore cannot act as the statutory escrow vault for investor funds. Offshore (non-Spanish) EMIs may only access Spanish rails via PSD2 passporting, branch registration with Banco de España under Article 46 Directive (EU) 2015/2366, or by becoming a sponsored direct participant in SEPA Clearing. Post-Brexit UK EMIs retain no passport and are treated as third-country providers; they may offer ancillary collection accounts but cannot legally perform the escrow safeguarding function for an authorised Spanish ECSP.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% - the standard withholding rate applicable to dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders who do not act through a Spanish permanent establishment (Non-Resident Income Tax, TRLIRNR).

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Filing window opens on 1 July after the calendar fiscal year end and closes on 25 July (i.e. within 25 days after six months from tax-period close; non-calendar fiscal year-ends follow the six-month-plus-25-days rule)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Mandatory Master File and Local File become required when the SL's annual net turnover (importe neto de la cifra de negocios) equals or exceeds €10,000,000; a related-party transaction annual information return (Form 232) is also required where aggregate transactions with each related party exceed the applicable €250,000 per-type threshold.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not maintain a UAE/Cayman-style 'Economic Substance Regulation' statute, but tax residence, CFC and GAAR rules, together with the corporate veil doctrine, demand real local management, payroll, offices and operational decision-making for the SL. A booking-shell arrangement that lacks actual management can render the entity a tax resident of another jurisdiction or non-existent for tax purposes, and allows the tax authority to disregard the corporate form.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate Income Tax fraud / evasion

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% of the unduly unpaid tax for serious infractions, escalating to 100% where concealment or illegal evidence occurs; non-filing after a second request can trigger a fixed fine plus a proportional penalty. Criminal tax evasion exceeding €120,000 carries imprisonment of 1 to 4 years and a fine of at least twice the defrauded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held jointly and severally for unpaid corporate tax and social security debts where they intentionally caused or failed to prevent non-payment. For criminal evasion, personal imprisonment, fine, operation and travel bans, and disqualification from public subsidies and tax benefits may be imposed after conviction.
Unlicensed equity crowdfunding activity

Statutory sanction: CNMV sanctions may include suspension or revocation of the activity, fines that can reach several million euros, and public warning; unauthorised issuance is separately classified as a serious securities-market infraction.

Director personal liability: Directors, managers and beneficial owners of unauthorised platforms can be jointly fined by CNMV, ordered to cease operations, disqualified from acting as managers of listed or regulated financial firms, and prosecuted for fraud or misappropriation if investor assets were used for private benefit.
Money laundering / deficient AML compliance

Statutory sanction: Sanctions under Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering range from €300 up to €5,000,000 (or 10 times the illicit proceeds when exceeding the capped amount), plus suspension of authorisation; the conduct can constitute a money-laundering criminal offence carrying imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years depending on value and aggravating factors.

Director personal liability: Directors who fail to enforce AML controls may be personally fined and jointly liable for restoration; criminal money-laundering proceedings permit preventive attachment, travel bans and imprisonment of the natural persons. Corporate veil-piercing allows seizure of personal assets when the entity is a façade for illicit flows.
Transfer pricing and artificial attribution failure

Statutory sanction: The Spanish tax authority may adjust the transaction to arm's length, imputing additional taxable income with late-payment interest; a misleading valuation in related-party returns is subject to a proportional penalty (15% of the uncorrected adjustment value in general), and failure to file Form 232 carries fixed fines from €300 per infraction plus surcharges.

Director personal liability: Joint secondary liability attaches where directors proposed or approved a transaction knowing that the transfer-pricing system was fictitious. The concealment of real decision-making can lead to deeming the SL a substance-less conduit and re-characterising its income as taxable in the hands of the beneficial owner or the shareholders (piercing the corporate veil).
